title: Private tree by-law and taxi accessibility funding
subtitle: Debenture borrowing, Drill Hall future, municipal service agreements, TaxiSCRIP review and Vehicle for Hire by-law changes.
overview: Council updated Guelph's Private Tree Protection By-law, replacing the 2010 version. A proposal to protect smaller trees, at 10 centimetres on larger lots and 40 centimetres elsewhere, was defeated {{vote:m9}}. The staff-recommended version passed {{vote:m11}}, with a report due by Q3 2027 on permit volumes, staff workloads and canopy results. Council also asked staff to report on a canopy conservation plan within the updated Urban Forest Management Plan {{vote:m12}}.

Council approved $39,500 from the Vehicle for Hire Accessibility Fund to help Red Top Taxi convert a vehicle for wheelchair use {{vote:m13}}. The fund comes from ride-share fees and had not been used before. Council then directed staff to review the TaxiSCRIP program and mobility transit applications {{vote:m16}}. It also asked staff to report on possible changes to the Vehicle for Hire Schedule of the Business Licensing By-law {{vote:m19}}.

A consent package also approved up to $118.15 million in debenture borrowing, a revised Municipal Service and Financing Agreements Policy, and keeping the Drill Hall as a city-owned asset while seeking a community partner for an arts and culture space. Council also passed a by-law recognizing contract awards for the Wyndham-Wellington water project funded by a provincial grant. The mayor marked the city's 198th birthday.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed the updated by-law and repealed the 2010 by-law, with staff to report on its effects by Q3 2027.
Council rejected a proposal to regulate trees over 10 centimetres on larger lots and over 40 centimetres on other lots.
Staff will report on a canopy conservation plan in the updated Urban Forest Management Plan, with a memo in the draft 2026 budget update.
Council approved $39,500 from the Vehicle for Hire Accessibility Fund to modify one vehicle for wheelchair accessibility.
Staff will review the TaxiSCRIP program and mobility transit applications through the 2026 budget confirmation process, with feedback from the Accessibility Advisory Committee.
Staff will report back on possible changes to the Vehicle for Hire Schedule of the Business Licensing By-law to make best use of the fund for accessible mobility.
The city will keep the Drill Hall, seek capital funding and an open process to find a community partner for an arts and culture centre, and advocate to the province on residential permissions.
Council approved debt financing for listed capital projects, up to $118.15 million over terms of no more than 20 years.

debate: A delegate who is a certified arborist supported the original 50 centimetre threshold. The delegate argued that lower thresholds could discourage private tree planting and that money would be better spent on a rebate program for tree care.

Supporters of the 40 centimetre amendment called it a compromise and wanted a go-slow approach. Staff said any lower threshold would increase workload, budget needs and permit timelines. Opponents of lowering the threshold pointed to tree canopy goals, public engagement results and long-term savings from trees. {{vote:m9}}

On the Red Top request, supporters said the fund was set up seven years ago for vehicle modifications, that Red Top offers 24/7 and out-of-town service, and that council should follow the existing policy. Staff said the fund can only pay for vehicle modifications.

Delegates linked to the Accessibility Advisory Committee said the committee had voted against the request. They said the fund had been understood to support TaxiSCRIP, which they said has application barriers, and that a for-profit company should not receive it before a review. Another delegate supported the request, citing limited accessible taxis in winter.

One councillor said the fund might be better used for mobility transit. Others said the review and the funding request were separate issues, and the mayor said the review motions would follow the decision.
